description: A Product Director must approve the production rollout policy for a new offline-sync engine in the mobile application, including the initial audience, rollout size, observation period, customer exclusions, and data safeguards.

shared_context.S1: The new offline-sync engine is scheduled for a Wednesday production rollout.
shared_context.S2: The engine passed the planned functional and staging reliability tests.
shared_context.S3: Riley makes the binding decision on the production rollout policy.
shared_context.S4: The release-readiness routine requires mobile engineering, reliability, customer support, and privacy to give their final status before Riley records the rollout plan.
shared_context.S5: If a scheduled participant does not provide a status, Riley repeats that participant's turn before recording the plan so every function has a recorded final status.
shared_context.S6: The rollout worksheet records each eligible platform as a separate entry.

PF1.text: While reviewing a compatibility report for an unrelated mobile release, Maya confirmed that Android versions below 8.5 emit the legacy tombstone format that the new sync engine cannot reconcile. The approved first-rollout audience therefore includes iOS and Android 8.5 or newer, while Android versions below 8.5 are excluded. She has not updated the rollout document because the compatibility report was completed only this morning.

PF2.text: Jon measured the production sync queue during a traffic replay and confirmed that a rollout above 5 percent would exceed the queue's safe processing margin. He also confirmed that reliability needs a 30-minute observation period after enabling the flag, but he has not added those numbers to the release ticket yet.

PF3.text: Elena confirmed from current support cases that the Aurora and Helix enterprise accounts have active offline workflows and must be excluded from the first rollout until their account teams complete a separate acceptance check. She found this while preparing support coverage and has not posted the account list in the release channel.

PF4.text: Dev confirmed in a privacy review this afternoon that the sync payload can carry location metadata and that the first rollout must disable location metadata for every user until the data-use review is closed. The finding is not yet in the privacy tracking system because the review finished minutes ago.

acceptance_conditions: The initial rollout must be exactly 5 percent.
The rollout must remain under observation for exactly 30 minutes.
Eligible platforms must be exactly iOS and Android 8.5 or newer.
Aurora and Helix must be excluded from the first rollout.
Location metadata must be disabled for every user.

decisive_facts.why: The compatibility confirmation changes the eligible platform list from an unrestricted mobile audience to exactly iOS and Android 8.5+.
The queue measurement changes the rollout size to exactly 5 percent and the required observation period to exactly 30 minutes.
The support confirmation changes the first-rollout exclusion list to exactly Aurora and Helix.
The privacy finding changes the rollout safeguard to disabling location metadata for every user and supplies the fact that must be cited in the justification.
